outage_intro: One destination turned slow for 60 seconds while another tenant kept sending. This is the median of three retest runs. Per-destination limits held the healthy tenant's p99 at 61 ms. With them removed it reached 36,317 ms, about 599 times worse. The failing destination caught up 25 seconds after it recovered. The first attempt at this test missed the 250 ms budget in 2 of 3 runs, because of one second stalls that also hit before the outage began.
evidence_intro: A clean result only means something if the test could have failed. So each claim below is paired with a control that must fail. The plan was committed before the runs, and the tests that failed are shown here too.

design.title: Nothing is sent before it is durable
design.text: A worker commits its lease before the request leaves, so a crash at any line can be recovered.

design.title: A late worker cannot change anything
design.text: Each claim gets a new token. A worker that wakes after its lease ended is recorded, and ignored.

design.title: One key, across every retry
design.text: The receiver commits the key and the expense in one transaction, so a resend finds the key and writes nothing.

design.title: One bad destination stays contained
design.text: Limits are derived from leased rows, so a crash cannot leave them wrong, and a breaker stops wasted attempts.

design.title: An acknowledged event outlives its primary
design.text: With synchronous replication, ingress answers only after the standby has the commit.

scope: All numbers were measured on one Apple M5 Pro Mac, with PostgreSQL 17 flushing the drive cache on every commit. The load generator, engine, receiver and databases shared that machine and one drive, and other work ran on it too.

The cause of the stalls at 2,000 per second was not found. A drive flush probe stayed fast through the retest, so a slow flush does not explain them there. A rate that holds for 60 seconds and fails at ten minutes is a real finding.

The fault model is process death, lost responses and pauses. Power loss was not tested, and the failovers share one machine, so they say nothing about a data centre failure. Promotion is triggered by the harness, with a declared 2 second detection time.
provenance: This is an offline replay of recorded runs. All data is synthetic.
